Synthetic difference-in-differences estimation and inference

Source: R/sdid.R
sdid.Rd

Estimates the average effect of a treatment on the treated from a balanced panel in long format, with its standard error, in the manner of the Stata command sdid of Clarke et al. (2024). The design is detected from the treatment column. If every treated unit adopts treatment in the same period, the estimator is applied to the panel as a whole. If adoption is staggered, each adoption cohort, meaning the units that first adopt treatment in one period together with the units never treated, is estimated separately, and the overall effect averages the cohort effects with weights proportional to each cohort's number of treated units times its number of post-treatment periods.

Usage

sdid(
  data,
  outcome,
  unit,
  time,
  treatment,
  vce,
  covariates = NULL,
  method = c("sdid", "sc", "did"),
  reps = 50,
  seed = NULL,
  level = 95,
  alternative = c("two.sided", "greater", "less"),
  covariate.method = c("optimized", "projected"),
  standardize = TRUE,
  projection.sample = c("controls", "untreated"),
  num.threads = NULL,
  graph = TRUE,
  quietly = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A balanced panel in long format, with one row per unit and period. A data frame, tibble or data.table.

outcome, unit, time, treatment

Names of the columns holding the outcome, the unit identifier, the period and the treatment indicator. The indicator is 1 for a treated unit from its first treated period onward and 0 otherwise. Units first treated in the same period form a cohort, and if not every treated unit is first treated in the same period, the design is staggered.

vce

The method of inference, which must be given. "bootstrap" resamples units, and "placebo" gives units never treated the treatment pattern of the treated units, both over reps replications. "jackknife" leaves out one unit at a time with the weights held fixed. "noinference" skips inference. The bootstrap and the jackknife need more than one treated unit, and for a staggered design the jackknife needs more than one in every cohort. The placebo needs more units never treated than treated.

covariates

Optional names of numeric columns of time-varying covariates to adjust for. Defaults to NULL, adjusting for none.

method

The estimator. "sdid" (the default) for synthetic difference-in-differences, "sc" for synthetic control or "did" for difference-in-differences.

reps

The number of bootstrap or placebo replications. Defaults to 50, as in the Stata command. More give a more precise standard error.

seed

An optional seed for the replications, so that results can be reproduced. It applies within this call only, and the state of the random number generator is restored afterward. Defaults to NULL.

level

The confidence level of the intervals, in percent. Defaults to 95.

alternative

The alternative hypothesis of the test of the effect against zero. "two.sided" (the default) tests whether the effect differs from zero, "greater" whether it is positive and "less" whether it is negative. A one-sided test gives one-sided p-values and intervals open in its direction, so that level = 95 corresponds to a one-sided test at 5%. Choose the direction before seeing the estimate. The estimate and its standard error are the same under every alternative.

covariate.method

How the covariates are adjusted for, ignored without covariates. "optimized" (the default) estimates their coefficients jointly with the weights. "projected" first regresses the outcome on the covariates and fixed effects, then estimates on the adjusted outcome, as Kranz (2022) proposes.

standardize

For the optimized method, TRUE (the default) to scale each covariate to mean zero and standard deviation one while solving, which keeps covariates on very different scales from stalling the solver. Coefficients are reported in the covariates' own units either way.

projection.sample

For the projected method, the observations its regression uses. "controls" (the default) uses the units never treated in every period, as the Stata command does. "untreated" adds the treated units' periods before treatment, a larger sample that assumes the treatment had no effect before it began.

num.threads

The number of threads for the replications. Defaults to NULL, which uses the option sdid.num.threads if it is set and every available thread otherwise. Results do not depend on it.

graph

TRUE (the default) to draw the trends plot of the estimate, as sdid_plot(fit) would.

quietly

TRUE to print nothing, for example within a loop. Defaults to FALSE, which prints, as the Stata command does, a header describing the data and the inference before estimating, the progress of any replications, then the results, whether or not the result is assigned. It does not affect graph.

...

Further settings of the estimator, such as zeta.omega and zeta.lambda, the regularization of the unit and time weights, max.iter, the most iterations of their solver, and sparsify, which sets small unit weights to zero.

Value

Invisibly, a list of class "sdid", which prints as the tables sdid() prints. Its methods, described in sdid-methods, and weights.sdid() are the stable way to extract results. Its components are as follows.

estimate

The estimated average treatment effect on the treated. For a staggered design, the average of the cohorts' effects with the weights in cohorts.

se

Its standard error. It is NA without inference, and for the jackknife when it is not defined, as when a cohort's unit weights rest on a single control.

z

The z statistic, estimate / se.

p.value

The p-value of z under the standard normal distribution, against alternative.

conf.int

The lower and upper bounds of the normal confidence interval at level. A one-sided test's interval is open in the direction of its alternative, with an infinite bound.

level

The confidence level, in percent.

alternative

The alternative hypothesis, "two.sided", "greater" or "less".

vce

The inference method.

reps

The number of bootstrap or placebo replications, or NA for the jackknife and without inference.

method

The estimator, "sdid", "sc" or "did".

design

"block" when every treated unit adopts treatment in the same period, and "staggered" otherwise.

cohorts

A data frame with a row per adoption period. period is the adoption period as it appears in the time column, treated its number of treated units, post its number of periods from adoption on, weight its share of the overall effect, proportional to treated times post, estimate its effect, se its standard error, and z, p.value, conf.low and conf.high its z statistic, p-value and confidence interval, computed as the overall effect's. A block design has one row, with a weight of 1. The bootstrap and placebo compute a cohort's standard error over the replications in which it appears, and the jackknife over all units left out, as the Stata command does. Without inference the standard errors are NA.

estimates

A list of the underlying estimate of each cohort, named by adoption period, which the plot functions draw. Their structure is internal and may change, so weights.sdid() is the way to obtain the weights.

beta

The coefficients on the covariates, in the covariates' own units, named by covariate, or NULL without covariates. With the optimized method and staggered adoption, each cohort has its own coefficients, given as a matrix with a row per covariate and a column per adoption period. With the projected method all cohorts share one set of coefficients.

setup

The panel as matrices, with units never treated first. Y is the outcome and W the treatment indicator, each with a row per unit and a column per period. X, present with covariates, is an array with a third dimension per covariate. N0 is the number of units never treated and T0 the number of periods before treatment, which is NA for a staggered design. A staggered design adds adoption, each unit's adoption period as a column of Y, NA for units never treated, cohorts, the adoption periods as columns of Y, and staggered, which is TRUE.

variables

A list of the column names given as outcome, unit, time, treatment and covariates.

covariate.method

The covariate method used, or NULL without covariates.

call

The call.

Details

The result can be passed to the plot functions sdid_plot, sdid_units_plot and sdid_placebo_plot, and to sdid_placebo for an in-time placebo test. For a staggered design, the plots show one panel per cohort.

References

Damian Clarke, Daniel Pailañir, Susan Athey, and Guido Imbens. "On Synthetic Difference-in-Differences and Related Estimation Methods in Stata". The Stata Journal 24(4), 557-598, 2024.

Dmitry Arkhangelsky, Susan Athey, David A. Hirshberg, Guido W. Imbens, and Stefan Wager. "Synthetic Difference in Differences". American Economic Review 111(12), 4088-4118, 2021.

Examples

# \donttest{
data(california_prop99)
fit = sdid(california_prop99, "PacksPerCapita", "State", "Year",
           "treated", vce = "placebo", seed = 1213, graph = FALSE)
#> 
#> Synthetic Difference-in-Differences Estimator
#> 
#> Outcome     PacksPerCapita
#> Treatment   treated
#> Units       39 (38 never treated, 1 treated)
#> Periods     31 (1970 to 2000), treatment from 1989
#> Inference   placebo, 50 replications
#> 
#> 
#>               ATT Std. Err.     z P>|z| [95% Conf. Interval]
#> treated -15.60383  10.93638 -1.43 0.154  -37.03873   5.83108
#> 
#> 95% confidence intervals and p-values use the normal approximation.
confint(fit, level = 0.9)
#>               5 %     95 %
#> treated -33.59257 2.384911
# }
